14: // GraphNodeAttachResourceConfig is an interface that must be implemented by nodes
15: // that want resource configurations attached.
16: type GraphNodeAttachResourceConfig interface {
17: 	GraphNodeConfigResource
18: 
19: 	// Sets the configuration, either to a present resource block or to
20: 	// a "removed" block commemorating a resource that has since been
21: 	// removed. Callers should always leave at least one of these
22: 	// arguments set to nil.
23: 	AttachResourceConfig(*configs.Resource, *configs.Removed)
24: }

26: // AttachResourceConfigTransformer goes through the graph and attaches
27: // resource configuration structures to nodes that implement
28: // GraphNodeAttachManagedResourceConfig or GraphNodeAttachDataResourceConfig.
29: //
30: // The attached configuration structures are directly from the configuration.
31: // If they're going to be modified, a copy should be made.
32: type AttachResourceConfigTransformer struct {
33: 	Config *configs.Config // Config is the root node in the config tree
34: }
35: 
36: func (t *AttachResourceConfigTransformer) Transform(g *Graph) error {
37: 
38: 	// Go through and find GraphNodeAttachResource
39: 	for _, v := range g.Vertices() {
40: 		// Only care about GraphNodeAttachResource implementations
41: 		arn, ok := v.(GraphNodeAttachResourceConfig)
42: 		if !ok {
43: 			continue
44: 		}
45: 
46: 		// Determine what we're looking for
47: 		addr := arn.ResourceAddr()
48: 
49: 		// Get the configuration.
50: 		config := t.Config.Descendent(addr.Module)
51: 
52: 		if config == nil {
53: 			log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: %q (%T) has no configuration available", dag.VertexName(v), v)
54: 			continue
55: 		}
56: 
57: 		if r := config.Module.ResourceByAddr(addr.Resource); r != nil {
58: 			log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: attaching to %q (%T) config from %#v", dag.VertexName(v), v, r.DeclRange)
59: 			arn.AttachResourceConfig(r, nil)
60: 			if t.hasConfigConditions(addr.Module, addr.Resource) {
61: 				log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: %q has configuration conditions", dag.VertexName(v))
62: 			}
63: 			if gnapmc, ok := v.(GraphNodeAttachProviderMetaConfigs); ok {
64: 				log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: attaching provider meta configs to %s", dag.VertexName(v))
65: 				if config.Module.ProviderMetas != nil {
66: 					gnapmc.AttachProviderMetaConfigs(config.Module.ProviderMetas)
67: 				} else {
68: 					log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: no provider meta configs available to attach to %s", dag.VertexName(v))
69: 				}
70: 			}
71: 		}
72: 
73: 		for _, r := range config.Module.Removed {
74: 			crAddr, ok := r.From.RelSubject.(addrs.ConfigResource)
75: 			if !ok {
76: 				// Not for a resource at all, so can't possibly match
77: 				continue
78: 			}
79: 			rAddr := crAddr.Resource
80: 			if rAddr != addr.Resource {
81: 				// Not the same resource
82: 				continue
83: 			}
84: 
85: 			log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: attaching to %q (%T) removed block from %#v", dag.VertexName(v), v, r.DeclRange)
86: 
87: 			// Validation ensures that there can't be both a resource/data block
88: 			// and a removed block referring to the same configuration, so
89: 			// we can assume that this isn't clobbering a non-removed resource
90: 			// configuration we already attached above.
91: 			arn.AttachResourceConfig(nil, r)
92: 		}
93: 	}
94: 
95: 	return nil
96: }

98: // hasConfigConditions reports whether the configuration for the given resource
99: // declares preconditions or postconditions. The lookup walks the module tree
100: // owned by the attached configuration, so this transformer can answer the same
101: // question while attaching resource configuration to the graph.
102: func (t *AttachResourceConfigTransformer) hasConfigConditions(module addrs.Module, resource addrs.Resource) bool {
103: 	if t.Config == nil {
104: 		return false
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	cfg := t.Config
108: 	for _, name := range module {
109: 		child, ok := cfg.Children[name]
110: 		if !ok || child == nil {
111: 			return false
112: 		}
113: 		cfg = child
114: 	}
115: 
116: 	if !cfg.Path.Equal(module) {
117: 		return false
118: 	}
119: 
120: 	mod := cfg.Module
121: 	if mod == nil {
122: 		return false
123: 	}
124: 
125: 	key := resource.String()
126: 	res := mod.ManagedResources[key]
127: 	if res == nil {
128: 		res = mod.DataResources[key]
129: 	}
130: 	if res == nil {
131: 		return false
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	switch res.Mode {
135: 	case addrs.ManagedResourceMode, addrs.DataResourceMode:
136: 		return len(res.Preconditions) > 0 || len(res.Postconditions) > 0
137: 	default:
138: 		return false
139: 	}
140: }

12: // of decoding an HCL traversal representing a relative path from the current
13: // module to a removeable object.
14: //
15: // Remove targets are somewhat simpler than move endpoints, in that they deal
16: // only with resources and modules defined in configuration, not instances of
17: // those objects as recorded in state. We are therefore able to determine the
18: // ConfigMoveable up front, since specifying any resource or module instance key
19: // in a removed block is invalid.
20: //
21: // An interesting quirk of RemoveTarget is that RelSubject denotes a
22: // configuration object that, if the removed block is valid, should no longer
23: // exist in configuration. This "last known address" is used to locate and delete
24: // the appropriate state objects, or, in the case in which the user has forgotten
25: // to remove the object from configuration, to report the address of that block
26: // in an error diagnostic.
27: type RemoveTarget struct {
28: 	// SourceRange is the location of the target address in configuration.
29: 	SourceRange tfdiags.SourceRange
30: 
31: 	// RelSubject, like MoveEndpoint's relSubject, abuses an absolute address
32: 	// type to represent a relative address.
33: 	RelSubject ConfigMoveable
34: }
35: 
36: func (t *RemoveTarget) ObjectKind() RemoveTargetKind {
37: 	return removeTargetKind(t.RelSubject)
38: }
39: 
40: func (t *RemoveTarget) String() string {
41: 	if t.ObjectKind() == RemoveTargetModule {
42: 		return t.RelSubject.(Module).String()
43: 	} else if t.ObjectKind() == RemoveTargetResource {
44: 		return t.RelSubject.(ConfigResource).String()
45: 	}
46: 	// No other valid address types
47: 	panic("Usupported remove target kind")
48: }
49: 
50: func (t *RemoveTarget) Equal(other *RemoveTarget) bool {
51: 	switch {
52: 	case (t == nil) != (other == nil):
53: 		return false
54: 	case t == nil:
55: 		return true
56: 	default:
57: 		// We can safely compare string representations, since the Subject is a
58: 		// simple module or resource address.
59: 		return t.String() == other.String() && t.SourceRange == other.SourceRange
60: 	}
61: }
62: 
63: func ParseRemoveTarget(traversal hcl.Traversal) (*RemoveTarget, tfdiags.Diagnostics) {
64: 	path, remain, diags := parseModulePrefix(traversal)
65: 	if diags.HasErrors() {
66: 		return nil, diags
67: 	}
68: 
69: 	rng := tfdiags.SourceRangeFromHCL(traversal.SourceRange())
70: 
71: 	if len(remain) == 0 {
72: 		return &RemoveTarget{
73: 			RelSubject:  path,
74: 			SourceRange: rng,
75: 		}, diags
76: 	}
77: 
78: 	rAddr, moreDiags := parseConfigResourceUnderModule(path, remain)
79: 	diags = diags.Append(moreDiags)
80: 	if diags.HasErrors() {
81: 		return nil, diags
82: 	}
83: 
84: 	if rAddr.Resource.Mode == DataResourceMode {
85: 		diags = diags.Append(&hcl.Diagnostic{
86: 			Severity: hcl.DiagError,
87: 			Summary:  "Data source address not allowed",
88: 			Detail:   "Data sources are never destroyed, so they are not valid targets of removed blocks. To remove the data source from state, remove the data source block from configuration.",
89: 			Subject:  rng.ToHCL().Ptr(),
90: 		})
91: 	}
92: 
93: 	return &RemoveTarget{
94: 		RelSubject:  rAddr,
95: 		SourceRange: rng,
96: 	}, diags
97: }

16: // RemoveStatement is the fully-specified form of addrs.Remove

18: 	// From is the absolute address of the configuration object being removed.
19: 	From addrs.ConfigMoveable
20: 
21: 	// Destroy indicates that the resource should be destroyed, not just removed
22: 	// from state.
23: 	Destroy   bool
24: 	DeclRange tfdiags.SourceRange
25: }
26: 
27: // FindRemoveStatements recurses through the modules of the given configuration
28: // and returns a set of all "removed" blocks defined within after deduplication
29: // on the From address.
30: //
31: // Error diagnostics are returned if any resource or module targeted by a remove
32: // block is still defined in configuration.
33: //
34: // A "removed" block in a parent module overrides a removed block in a child
35: // module when both target the same configuration object.
36: func FindRemoveStatements(rootCfg *configs.Config) (addrs.Map[addrs.ConfigMoveable, RemoveStatement], tfdiags.Diagnostics) {
37: 	stmts := findRemoveStatements(rootCfg, addrs.MakeMap[addrs.ConfigMoveable, RemoveStatement]())
38: 	diags := validateRemoveStatements(rootCfg, stmts)
39: 	return stmts, diags
40: }
41: 
42: func validateRemoveStatements(cfg *configs.Config, stmts addrs.Map[addrs.ConfigMoveable, RemoveStatement]) (diags tfdiags.Diagnostics) {
43: 	for _, rst := range stmts.Keys() {
44: 		switch rst := rst.(type) {
45: 		case addrs.ConfigResource:
46: 			m := cfg.Descendent(rst.Module)
47: 			if m == nil {
48: 				break
49: 			}
50: 
51: 			if r := m.Module.ResourceByAddr(rst.Resource); r != nil {
52: 				diags = diags.Append(&hcl.Diagnostic{
53: 					Severity: hcl.DiagError,
54: 					Summary:  "Removed resource still exists",
55: 					Detail:   fmt.Sprintf("This statement declares that %s was removed, but it is still declared in configuration.", rst),
56: 					Subject:  r.DeclRange.Ptr(),
57: 				})
58: 			}
59: 		case addrs.Module:
60: 			if m := cfg.Descendent(rst); m != nil {
61: 				diags = diags.Append(&hcl.Diagnostic{
62: 					Severity: hcl.DiagError,
63: 					Summary:  "Removed module still exists",
64: 					Detail:   fmt.Sprintf("This statement declares that %s was removed, but it is still declared in configuration.", rst),
65: 					Subject:  m.CallRange.Ptr(),
66: 				})
67: 			}
68: 		}
69: 	}
70: 	return diags
71: }

75: 		switch mc.From.ObjectKind() {
76: 		case addrs.RemoveTargetResource:
77: 			// First, stitch together the module path and the RelSubject to form
78: 			// the absolute address of the config object being removed.
79: 			res := mc.From.RelSubject.(addrs.ConfigResource)
80: 			fromAddr := addrs.ConfigResource{
81: 				Module:   append(cfg.Path, res.Module...),
82: 				Resource: res.Resource,
83: 			}
84: 
85: 			// If we already have a remove statement for this ConfigResource, it
86: 			// must have come from a parent module, because duplicate removed
87: 			// blocks in the same module are ignored during parsing.
88: 			// The removed block in the parent module overrides the block in the
89: 			// child module.
90: 			existingStatement, ok := into.GetOk(fromAddr)
91: 			if ok {
92: 				if existingResource, ok := existingStatement.From.(addrs.ConfigResource); ok &&
93: 					existingResource.Equal(fromAddr) {
94: 					continue
95: 				}
96: 			}
97: 
98: 			into.Put(fromAddr, RemoveStatement{
99: 				From:      fromAddr,
100: 				Destroy:   mc.Destroy,
101: 				DeclRange: tfdiags.SourceRangeFromHCL(mc.DeclRange),
102: 			})
103: 		case addrs.RemoveTargetModule:
104: 			// First, stitch together the module path and the RelSubject to form
105: 			// the absolute address of the config object being removed.
106: 			mod := mc.From.RelSubject.(addrs.Module)
107: 			absMod := append(cfg.Path, mod...)
108: 
109: 			// If there is already a statement for this Module, it must
110: 			// have come from a parent module, because duplicate removed blocks
111: 			// in the same module are ignored during parsing.
112: 			// The removed block in the parent module overrides the block in the
113: 			// child module.
114: 			existingStatement, ok := into.GetOk(mc.From.RelSubject)
115: 			if ok {
116: 				if existingModule, ok := existingStatement.From.(addrs.Module); ok &&
117: 					existingModule.Equal(absMod) {
118: 					continue
119: 				}
120: 			}
121: 
122: 			into.Put(absMod, RemoveStatement{
123: 				From:      absMod,
124: 				Destroy:   mc.Destroy,
125: 				DeclRange: tfdiags.SourceRangeFromHCL(mc.DeclRange),
126: 			})
127: 		default:
128: 			panic("Unsupported remove target kind")
129: 		}
130: 	}
131: 
132: 	for _, childCfg := range cfg.Children {
133: 		into = findRemoveStatements(childCfg, into)
134: 	}
135: 
136: 	return into

part.text:
Implemented the fix.

The bug was in `AttachResourceConfigTransformer`: it only looked for `removed` blocks in the resource's own module, and skipped entirely when that module no longer existed in configuration. A root-level `removed { from = module.null.null_resource.main ... }` therefore never had its provisioners attached.

The transformer now searches ancestor modules along the target resource's path, resolving each removed block relative to the module where it is declared. This also handles modules that have been removed from configuration entirely.

Validated with the failing test and the full `internal/terraform` package:

```
go test ./internal/terraform -run TestContext2Apply_provisionerDestroyRemoved
go test ./internal/terraform
```

Both pass.
